fields.description: CI run history (2026-10-05..2026-11-02, 258 runs) averages ~228 runner-min/day. 43 of 46 PR merges re-ran the full Rust suite on master for a tree the PR run had already passed (push runs: ~65 min/day). The macOS Rust 1.94.0 leg (~18 min/day) repeats OS-independent MSRV compilation already covered by Linux verify. Native Runlimit PostgreSQL runs on two toolchains for every change although 24 of 35 master commits touched none of its inputs (~16 min/day).
fields.acceptance_criteria: 1) A push to master skips Rust test steps only when a same-repository pull_request/merge_group run of ci.yml recorded the exact tree after every test job passed, and the master Rust cache is an exact hit; any failure to prove that runs the full job. 2) macOS subprocess job runs once on the pinned toolchain; Rust 1.94.0 stays covered by Linux verify. 3) Native Runlimit PostgreSQL runs once on the pinned toolchain, only when its local dependency closure or global build inputs change; a failed plan runs it. 4) Planner has unit tests; docs/testing.md and evidence statements describe the new scope.
fields.title: Cut duplicate Rust CI work: verified master pushes, pinned-only macOS, scoped Runlimit PostgreSQL

data.text: PR #75 (branch ci/cut-duplicate-runs-f0jz, commit 944767d). fields.description: Every package declares rust-version 1.94 (SQLx 0.9.0's floor) and CI runs the full verify job on both 1.94.0 and 1.98.1 (~18 runner-min per run, ~60/day). Over 360 runs the 1.94.0 job failed alone twice, one a real compile break (use super as catalog; on 2026-09-26). The owner chose to raise the minimum to the pinned toolchain before first publication and drop the second job.
fields.acceptance_criteria: 1) Every published-candidate and example package declares the pinned toolchain as rust-version; evidence snapshots stay unchanged. 2) CI verify runs once on the pinned toolchain (weekly stable unchanged); the at-rest portability gate uses the same toolchain. 3) AGENTS.md, README and docs state the single-toolchain policy and what a pin bump requires. 4) Complete scripts/verify.sh passes on the pinned toolchain with any newly enabled MSRV-gated lints fixed. 5) The stale 'hosted push reuse unverified' status row from batter-f0jz is updated.

fields.title: Make outbound refusal fixtures deterministic on macOS

data.text: On Darwin arm64, scripts/verify.sh fails outbound_exchange::a_refused_connection_proves_the_mutation_unsent_and_releases_the_fence (NotDispatched TimedOut instead of Failed) and only_outcomes_that_prove_nothing_was_sent_release_the_fence (unknown.deadline). Both hold a TcpSocket bound without listen. Standalone Python socket bind/connect with 200ms timeout reproduces timeout for IPv4 and IPv6; dropping a listener produces ConnectionRefused but loses the reservation. Preserve deterministic port ownership and exact semantic assertions in a portable Unix fixture; do not simply loosen the expected classification. Also inspect crates/batter-outbound-http/tests/support/peer.rs RefusingPort and its consumers.

Implemented both refusal helpers using an explicitly bound client socket connected to a fixture listener; retain both stream endpoints and target client local port. Setup bounded to two seconds. Existing exact Failed/non-dispatch/fence assertions unchanged; regression checks reject non-reuse rebind and verify retained connection carries only the marker after exchange. Focused example 7 tests and leaf before_head/redaction 17 tests pass on macOS arm64. Leaf before_head/redaction also passed in Linux Docker with Rust 1.98.1. No public API changes. Full verification rerun started.

fields.title: Migrate remaining reqwest users to 0.13 preserving TLS policy

data.text: Migrated both reqwest 0.12 users to 0.13.5 with explicit ring rustls configs, bundled webpki-roots 1.0.11, TLS 1.2/1.3 and fixed HTTP/1.1. No global provider or platform trust.
